key_insight: Applying randomized smoothing directly in the model's feature space (Feature-space Smoothing, FS) yields provable, certified robustness for multimodal LLMs by stabilizing their internal feature representations against adversarial perturbations.
problem_solved: Multimodal LLMs are vulnerable to adversarial perturbations that distort feature representations and cause incorrect predictions; this paper provides a method to provably defend those internal features.
method: Transform any pretrained feature encoder into a smoothed variant by applying controlled randomness/noise in feature space to obtain stable feature outputs.
Derive theoretical guarantees (certified robustness bounds) that quantify how much feature-space perturbation can be tolerated without changing downstream predictions.
Deploy the smoothed encoder in existing multimodal LLM pipelines to improve resistance to adversarial distortions without redesigning the whole model.
impact: Provides AI practitioners a principled, plug-and-play defense to make multimodal models more reliable and auditable under adversarial attacks, enabling safer deployment in vision-language tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input image/text → feature encoder → FS (noise injection in feature space) → multimodal LLM → prediction (showing 'smoothed' path).
Feature-space geometry: scatter plots showing original features (sensitive) vs. smoothed features (concentrated/robust) with certification radius circles.
Certification bar chart: certified radius / robustness probability before vs. after applying FS across multiple perturbation magnitudes.
Threat vs. defense illustration: an adversarial perturbation altering input vs. FS-blocked feature change, with a short caption summarizing the theoretical guarantee.
paper_title: Provable Robustness in Multimodal Large Language Models via Feature Space Smoothing
paper_authors: Song Xia, Meiwen Ding, Chenqi Kong, Wenhan Yang, Xudong Jiang
